messages:
Alex Kim: Heads up — found a nasty edge where streaming generator never closes if you cancel right after an auth-refresh. Repro in sample-app with short lived tokens. :frowning_face:
Marta Ruiz: can you paste the minimal repro?
Alex Kim: yep — gist (shortened):
```
client = RedwoodClient(token=short_lived)
stream = client.chat.stream(...)
for chunk in stream:
    if should_abort():
        stream.aclose()  # or .cancel()
        break
```
But if the token refresh happens concurrently (401 -> refresh -> retry), the underlying socket stays open and the async generator finalizer doesn't run.
Kevin Zhao: that sounds like the weakref/finalizer race we saw before, but this is with token refresh + retry layer involved.
Samir Patel: did you try explicit `await stream.aclose()` vs `break`? IIRC `break` lets the generator finalizer run, but if there's a pending retry it can re-attach the socket.
Alex Kim: explicit aclose sometimes works, sometimes doesn't. I added a small repro that toggles a race via sleep. Logging shows: `SSE connection created -> token refresh -> retry -> cancel called -> socket still open`.
Lee Chen: could be two cancellation paths: SDK-level cancel vs underlying aiohttp/requests close. Also typing mismatch: public API annotated as `Iterator[ChatEvent]` for sync but returns a contextmanager-like object. We should consider adding a sync contextmanager `with client.stream(...) as s:` so users don't rely on gc/finalizers.
Marta Ruiz: agree on API ergonomics. Filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/842 (devex/stream-cancel-repro).
ci-bot: Issue #842 created by mruiz — labels: sdk, bug, p1.
Samir Patel: I pushed a small workaround branch that forces immediate socket close on cancel and cancels any pending retry futures: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1934. It's hacky but reduces repro rate.
Kevin Zhao: can you add a unit test that simulates refresh+retry during iteration? We should add deterministic sleeps or a mock clock.
Samir Patel: added test + notes. Still flaky on Windows, probably because loop scheduling is different.
Alex Kim: repro steps I used locally:
1) create token that expires in 1s
2) start streaming large response
3) call cancel around 1.2s after start
4) observe socket fd in TIME_WAIT for a while and generator finalizer logged later.
Also hitting typing confusion in examples — tutorial shows `for chunk in client.chat.stream(...)` but the function is async; beginners try to use sync loop and get silent resource leak.
Marta Ruiz: we should update docs with explicit async example + add a synchronous wrapper that spawns an internal loop and closes properly.
Lee Chen: filing a small DX task to add `Stream` context manager and improve typings in stubs, plus sample-app change and a migration note. Assigning to @samir and @kevin.
Kevin Zhao: I'll take the typing/stubs work. Will change return types to `AsyncIterator[ChatChunk]` and export a `sync_stream()` helper which yields same chunks but manages lifecycle.
Alex Kim: thanks — that will unblock our sample-app. Also, could we add an option `force_close_on_cancel=True` defaulting to False to avoid surprising behavior?
Samir Patel: added knob in branch; default False for compatibility but will flip after a short deprecation.
Marta Ruiz: plan for rollout: ship tests + fix to main branch, update docs/examples, add changelog note, then turn on feature flag in Canary.
Alex Kim: awesome. marking this repro as blocked-on-pr #1934 and typing PR. :+1:
